verdict.rationale: Stripe's own docs say Terminal supports building a custom POS integration, including an 'API-based integration' alongside the SDKs. They also mention a 'server-driven integration' with a built-in simulated reader for testing, so the core capability is documented first-party. The pack does not show how the backend actually drives the reader (no endpoint or flow detail), so coverage of the story is only partial. missing for 10: documentation of the server-driven reader-control flow (e.g., API calls that send a payment to a reader from the backend), hands-on or independent corroboration of the server-driven API specifically.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a custom point-of-sale checkout that drives the terminal from my backend through a documented server-driven API

citations.quote: Build a custom POS integration tailored to your business. Terminal supports an API-based integration in addition to SDKs for Android, iOS, JavaScript, and React Native.
Stripe Terminal SDKs and server-driven integration come with a built-in simulated card reader, so you can develop and test your app without connecting to physical hardware.
you can use Terminal with no-code options, a custom point-of-sale (POS) integration, or supported third-party POS and gateway integrations
the ability to fully integrate with the API on a terminal level is the most powerful thing here, especially combined with Stripe Connect.
